changes.title: Group Project Meeting by video call

constraints: Training events are protected by the profile and remain unchanged at 07:00-09:00 and 16:30-18:30 on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
Sleep is protected as at least 8 hours per night. The proposed sleep moves keep 8-hour blocks while ending at 06:00 so the longer 60-minute morning commute can reach the HPC by 07:00.
The transport strike is the operational reason for extending each morning commute to the HPC from 25 minutes to 60 minutes.
Fixed/protected training is not moved. Sleep is only shifted earlier because the user explicitly allowed a slight earlier shift to preserve 8 hours during the strike.
Campus classes marked non-fixed are dropped during the strike and replaced with self-study blocks near HPC/home where the request supports study as the substitute activity.
The Thursday group project meeting involves peers and should be confirmed with them before relying on the video-call version, even though the event description says it can be joined by video call.
The deleted university commute events are operationally tied to campus attendance; because campus attendance is being avoided during the strike, keeping them would create unnecessary travel burden.
No opening hours, travel times beyond those supplied, or extra return journeys are invented.
priorities: Preserve all mandatory training sessions on time.
Preserve 8 hours of sleep every night covered by the calendar.
Avoid HPC-to-campus travel during the strike to prevent excessive commuting and preserve recovery energy.
Keep academic progress through independent study blocks instead of attending non-mandatory campus lectures.
Reduce Friday evening disruption by dropping the low-priority campus social event, supporting rest and the earlier sleep pattern around the strike period.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep Wednesday Statistics and Friday Microeconomics lectures in person.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This would require campus attendance during the strike and conflict with the user’s instruction to drop non-mandatory campus classes to stay near HPC/home.

alternatives_considered.option: Leave morning commute events at their original 25-minute duration.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The supplied strike information says the home-to-HPC commute increases to 60 minutes, so the original commute would not get the user to 07:00 training on time.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the 07:00 training sessions later instead of shifting sleep and commute earlier.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Training sessions are protected, fixed, and top priority, with coach participation; moving them would be more disruptive and is not allowed by the hard constraints.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep Thursday’s meeting as an in-person campus meeting.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That would preserve an avoidable HPC-to-campus trip during the strike; the calendar notes the meeting can be joined by video call, but peers still need to confirm the switch.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the Friday Student Union Barbecue.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is a low-priority campus social event during the strike and would work against the request to stay near HPC/home for rest and study.

rationale.summary: The proposal keeps all training intact, shifts each protected sleep block 30 minutes earlier to preserve a full 8 hours, and expands each morning commute to the strike-adjusted 60 minutes so arrival at HPC remains on time. Non-mandatory campus classes are removed and replaced with self-study near HPC/home. The Thursday group project is represented as a video-call version at the same time, but the user should confirm this with teammates before treating it as settled. The user should also confirm any class absence expectations or catch-up materials with instructors, and confirm that the physiotherapy appointment remains at the HPC as scheduled.
